newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Scores of new mines in southern Africa seek funds.
newsitem.headline: Scores of new mines in southern Africa seek funds.

text.p: An alliance of black and white mining interests outside the main mining companies plans an investment drive this week at the African Mining Conference in Cape Town, saying up to 50,000 jobs could be created in southern Africa.

The Southern African Developing Mining and Mineral Industry Exchange, or Demindex, said in a press statement it would be lobbying for international funds "to put scores of potentially rich small and medium-scale mines in production".
Mining ministers and officials from 26 African countries are due to attend the conference from February 5 to 7 along with executives of major mining corporations and financial institutions, it said.
"We have counted at least 27 new mining projects which show potential and which only need investor funding to get them started," Demindex CEO Rika Lorens was quoted as saying.
"At least 400 potential investors will be there and it's an ideal opportunity for us to canvass for investment support."
Former South African Mineral and Energy Affairs minister Pik Botha, is described as a "key figure" in the Demindex initiative.

"There is more potential for short-term job creation in the developing mining industry than perhaps anywhere else," Botha was quoted as saying. "Some estimates put the figure at 40,000 to 50,000 new jobs. But whatever it is it is certainly huge."
Demindex said it represented mining interests from the medium and small scale to "artisanal shovel-and-wheelbarrow" operations.
